Alex — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, details below and I'll loop in Security for access rules.

- Uptime SLO: 99.95% monthly availability for our Hosted API (regional).
- Latency SLOs: P95 <= 180ms for small request profiles (typical gen) and P95 <= 350ms for longer context/large-token responses (documented by model/proxy).
- Measurement: We record per-request success/failure and request latency at the routing layer (metric names: api.request.success, api.request.latency_ms). Aggregation windows: 1m rolling and 30d window for SLO evaluation (Calcuation: 30d rolling burn-rate & monthly evaluation point).

We can provide a read-only Grafana dashboard showing the last 90 days per-region. For procurement packages we typically attach: uptime_slo_definitions.pdf (SLOs, measurement, error budget policies) and a monthly_uptime_report CSV with the last 3 months.

If we fall short: our exception path is to open an incident with a formal RCA and remediation plan. For contract remedies we provide service credits per the SLA in the procurement agreement; for operational exceptions we provide logs, metric windows and KV-cache traces where relevant.

I don't want to guess at internal access policy — looping in Neha to confirm what read-only access looks like and what evidence we can expose.

Thanks for the ping. Short answer: yes, we can provide a constrained read-only view and a packet of evidence for exception cases, but there are a few controls and steps. Summary below.

1) Read-only dashboard access
- We can create a time-limited Grafana API key scoped to a dashboard or panel and restrict by IP range (customer-controlled IP allowlist) and expiry (default 14 days, extendable by request).
- For buyers in enterprise procurement we also support SSO (SAML) for persistent read-only accounts tied to the customer's IDP; that requires a draft SAML config exchange and a short security review (3–5 business days).

2) Data and redaction
- Dashboards surface aggregated metrics only (no raw request payloads). Metric names exposed: api.request.latency_ms, api.request.success, region. No PII.
- We will not share raw request logs or KV cache contents by default. For RCA we can provide time-windowed exports of anonymized metric series and truncated error traces.

3) Evidence for exceptions / SLO misses
- Our standard package includes: monthly_uptime_report.csv, the SLO definition PDF, timestamped metric dumps (CSV) for the incident window, and an executive RCA (PDF) if an incident meets internal severity thresholds.
- If legal requires deeper artifacts (e.g., request-level logs) we handle via a controlled egress path and a written request reviewed by Security & Legal.

4) Operational process
- Request starts with a support ticket (support@redwood.com) flagged as "Procurement Evidence". Security reviews within 48 hours; dashboard access usually provisioned within 2 business days for time-limited links.

5) Auditability
- All customer admin/readonly access creations are logged; we can provide audit entries (timestamped) for access provisioning upon request.

I've attached a short how-to for provisioning the read-only link (grafana_readonly_instructions.txt) and the canonical SLO definitions (uptime_slo_definitions.pdf). Marissa — please confirm these artifacts match the SLA language we plan to include in the MSA.

-Neha
